title: BlackCat Ransomware & Triple Extortion (Analysis & Tactics)

vulnerabilities: BlackCat is designed to disable or kill key processes and services (such as security solutions and backup agents) so that the normal protection mechanisms do not detect or block its malicious activity. This “protection failure” enables the ransomware to proceed with file encryption, data exfiltration, and even launching additional extortion techniques without interference.

The ransomware’s effectiveness is partly due to the poor isolation and inadequate control of privileges on victim systems. Organizations that do not enforce strict process and service permissions allow malicious actors to terminate legitimate security processes and services. This weak control over resource access facilitates lateral movement and enables the ransomware to disable critical defenses, ultimately contributing to a broader compromise of the targeted networks.

CVE-2023-38180 enabled attackers on the same network to trigger denial-of-service conditions against .NET applications/Visual Studio by exhausting resources without needing user privileges.

title: Everything You Need to Know About Silent Skimming

vulnerabilities: The attackers exploit a .NET insecure deserialization flaw (CVE-2019-18935 in Progress Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX) to trigger remote code execution on internet-facing servers.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Reliance on an outdated/vulnerable Telerik UI component with a known RCE flaw provides an easy initial access vector for attackers.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: Attackers are able to place and execute dangerous files (e.g., DLLs, HTA, webshells like bypass.aspx) on the server to stage payloads and maintain access.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)
vulnerabilities: Through the deserialization exploit and webshells, the adversary injects and executes arbitrary DLL code and scripts (VBScript/PowerShell) on the server.
Privilege-escalation tools (BadPotato, GodPotato, Juicy/SweetPotato, SharpToken) abuse token/privilege misconfigurations to elevate from service/user context to higher privileges (e.g., SYSTEM).
Weak access controls on internet-facing applications and server directories enable remote code execution, webshell deployment, and subsequent lateral/post-exploitation actions.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Compromised payment infrastructure allows scraping and exfiltration of billing and credit card data via attacker-controlled C2 and Cloudflare-based exfiltration channels.
The campaign persisted for over a year across regions, indicating inadequate detection and logging to identify webshell use, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration activities in a timely manner.

The Qlik flaws allow unauthorized actions (e.g., sending unauthorized requests, adding new admin users) without proper authorization checks.

CVE-2023-48365 represents a bypass of the original fix for CVE-2023-41265, indicating incomplete or ineffective mitigation that attackers could circumvent.

Pre-auth exploitation paths (e.g., parts of ProxyShell chain and vCenter RCE) allowed actions without proper authorization checks.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: External Control of File Name or Path
vulnerabilities: ProxyShell chain enabled attacker-controlled file write paths (e.g., dropping web shells/arbitrary file write on Exchange).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

Endpoint defenses were bypassed (e.g., PowerLess backdoor running PowerShell in-process via .NET to evade process-based detection), undermining protection controls.

Credentials were harvested with tools like Mimikatz/KPOT and reused (e.g., for RDP), reflecting weak protection of secrets in memory and at rest.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

vulnerabilities: The injected script created invisible input fields to trick browsers/password managers into autofilling stored credentials, facilitating credential theft.

title: FBI: Androxgh0st malware botnet steals AWS, Microsoft credentials

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
vulnerabilities: Apache HTTP Server CVE-2021-41773 allows path traversal to read files like .env and, in some configs, reach RCE-capable endpoints.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
vulnerabilities: PHPUnit CVE-2017-9841 (exposed eval-stdin) lets attackers inject and execute arbitrary PHP code, enabling web shell deployment.
Laravel CVE-2018-15133 enables unsafe deserialization leading to remote code execution.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory
vulnerabilities: Cloud credentials stored in .env within web-accessible directories can be fetched (e.g., via traversal or direct access), facilitating account takeover and abuse.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Leakage of AWS/O365/SendGrid/Twilio credentials from exposed .env files and misconfigurations provides attackers with usable secrets.
Laravel applications left in debug/testing mode in production expose environment details and secrets that aid compromise.
Default-allow URI configurations and insufficient restrictions let unauthorized requests hit sensitive paths or components.
Over-privileged AWS IAM credentials allow creation of new users/policies and launching instances once credentials are stolen.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Running outdated/vulnerable Apache, Laravel, or PHPUnit versions left known CVEs exploitable by the botnet.

title: Apple fixes first zero-day bug exploited in attacks this year

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
vulnerabilities: WebKit type confusion (CVE-2024-23222) in processing malicious web content, allowing attackers to trigger memory corruption and execute arbitrary code on iOS/macOS/tvOS/Safari.
WebKit out-of-bounds read (CVE-2023-42916) that can expose memory when handling crafted web content, aiding further exploitation.
WebKit memory corruption leading to arbitrary code execution (CVE-2023-42917), reportedly mitigated with improved locking, consistent with a UAF condition triggered by crafted web content.

title: Hackers start exploiting critical Atlassian Confluence RCE flaw

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Template Engine
vulnerabilities: Server-side template injection (SSTI) in Confluence endpoints lets unauthenticated attackers supply template expressions that the engine evaluates, enabling RCE.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
vulnerabilities: The template injection ultimately allows arbitrary code execution on the server (e.g., running commands like whoami), constituting remote code injection.
User-controlled input is not properly validated/neutralized before being embedded into the template context, enabling injection.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Organizations running outdated or out-of-support Confluence versions remain exposed to a known critical RCE flaw due to not updating to fixed releases.

title: Google fixes first actively exploited Chrome zero-day of 2024

vulnerabilities: CVE-2024-0519 in Chrome’s V8 lets a crafted page trigger reads past buffer boundaries, exposing memory contents, potentially bypassing ASLR, and causing crashes.
CVE-2024-0517 in V8 allows writing outside allocated buffers, enabling memory corruption and potential arbitrary code execution.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (Type Confusion)
vulnerabilities: CVE-2024-0518 in V8 causes objects to be treated as the wrong type, leading to memory corruption and possible code execution.

title: Citrix warns of new Netscaler zero-days exploited in attacks

vulnerabilities: Authenticated low-privileged users can trigger remote code execution via the management interface (CVE-2023-6548), indicating insufficient authorization checks on dangerous functionality.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)
vulnerabilities: Management-interface flaw enabling remote code execution on affected NetScaler versions (CVE-2023-6548), i.e., unintended execution of attacker-controlled code.
Gateway/AAA configuration allows crafted requests to cause denial-of-service on unpatched appliances (CVE-2023-6549).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
vulnerabilities: Exposing the NetScaler management interface to the internet and not segregating management traffic increases attack surface and enables exploitation.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Continued use of end-of-life NetScaler ADC/Gateway 12.1 versions lacking security updates, leaving known issues unpatched.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Prior “Citrix Bleed” (CVE-2023-4966) information disclosure used to hijack sessions and breach organizations.

title: Fortra warns of new critical GoAnywhere MFT auth bypass, patch now

vulnerabilities: CVE-2024-0204 allows unauthenticated access to the admin setup function (InitialAccountSetup.xhtml), enabling creation of new administrator accounts without requiring login.
Attackers can directly browse to the InitialAccountSetup.xhtml endpoint after deployment, bypassing normal navigation checks to reach the admin account creation flow.
The application fails to verify that a requester is authorized to perform the privileged action of creating an administrative account via the administration portal.

title: GitHub rotates keys to mitigate impact of credential-exposing flaw

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection')
vulnerabilities: CVE-2024-0200 unsafe reflection in GHES enabling remote code execution on unpatched servers.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Exploitation allowed access to production container environment variables containing credentials.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
vulnerabilities: CVE-2024-0507 command injection in the Enterprise Server Management Console.
Command injection allowed a Management Console user with editor role to escalate privileges.

title: Over 5,300 GitLab servers exposed to zero-click account takeover attacks

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
vulnerabilities: Password reset workflow allowed reset emails (tokens) to be sent to attacker-controlled addresses for a victim account, enabling zero-click account takeover.
The password reset endpoint accepted a JSON array of multiple email addresses instead of validating and enforcing a single, verified email, enabling abuse of the reset process.
The system failed to verify that the recipient email was an authorized/verified address for the target account before issuing a reset token.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: The password reset token/link (a sensitive authentication secret) was delivered to an attacker-controlled email address.
Accounts without 2FA were fully susceptible to takeover via the reset-token abuse, increasing impact even though the flaw did not bypass 2FA.
Organizations continued running vulnerable GitLab versions (pre-fixed releases), exposing internet-facing instances to a known critical flaw due to delayed patching.

title: Exploit released for Fortra GoAnywhere MFT auth bypass bug

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
vulnerabilities: Attackers use path traversal to access the /InitialAccountSetup.xhtml endpoint that should be inaccessible after setup.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel
vulnerabilities: By reaching the setup flow via an alternate path, attackers bypass normal authentication controls and gain access to privileged setup functionality.
The initial account setup page allows creation of an administrator account without enforcing authentication once it is reachable, enabling unauthorized admin user creation.

title: Kasseika ransomware uses antivirus driver to kill other antiviruses

vulnerabilities: Phished credentials alone were sufficient for initial access, indicating missing or ineffective MFA on corporate accounts.
Attackers used PsExec to execute scripts, create services, and move laterally across hosts, implying overly permissive remote admin/service creation controls.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: The attack chain downloads and loads Martini.sys at runtime, incorporating externally obtained code into the system’s trusted execution path.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: A known-vulnerable, signed kernel driver (Martini.sys/viragt64.sys) was allowed to load, indicating failure to blocklist or update components with known flaws (BYOVD).
The vulnerable driver exposes privileged kernel operations to user space, enabling termination of protected AV/EDR processes.
BYOVD typically abuses weak IOCTL handlers that do not validate user-supplied pointers/parameters in the driver, enabling arbitrary privileged actions.
Security controls (AV/EDR self-protection, driver blocklisting) were bypassed or ineffective, allowing the malware to disable defenses and proceed to encryption.
Adversaries cleared Windows event logs via wevtutil without resistance, indicating lack of tamper-resistant, centralized, or immutable logging.

title: Mastodon vulnerability allows attackers to take over accounts

vulnerabilities: Insufficient origin validation in Mastodon’s federation allowed attackers to make requests appear as if they came from trusted remote instances, enabling user impersonation and account takeover (CVE-2024-23832).
By spoofing the origin/identity of remote accounts or instances, attackers could bypass identity checks and take over accounts across instances (impact of CVE-2024-23832).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: The “TootRoot” flaw allowed crafted toots to create web shells on target servers, effectively enabling upload/creation of executable files in a web-accessible location leading to server compromise (CVE-2023-36460).

title: Russian hackers stole Microsoft corporate emails in month-long breach

vulnerabilities: The legacy test tenant account was guessable via password spraying, indicating inadequate password complexity/rotation policies.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
vulnerabilities: Lack of effective lockout/throttling allowed repeated password attempts across many accounts (password spray) without being blocked.
The compromised account was not protected with MFA/2FA, enabling takeover through password-only authentication.
A non-production test account appears to have had (or could obtain) privileges enabling access to corporate email accounts, violating least-privilege.
Weak segregation between the test tenant and production email resources allowed lateral movement/pivot to higher-value mailboxes.
Adversaries maintained access for over a month before detection, suggesting inadequate monitoring/alerting for anomalous authentication and mailbox access.

title: PurpleFox malware infects thousands of computers in Ukraine

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Users executed laced MSI installers (e.g., fake Telegram app) without verifying source integrity/signature, allowing initial compromise.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Systems running outdated OS/software were exploitable via known flaws, enabling PurpleFox self-propagation.
Password brute-forcing succeeded due to weak credentials on network-accessible services.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
vulnerabilities: Lack of lockout/throttling on authentication endpoints (e.g., SMB/RDP) facilitated brute-force propagation.
Flat networks without VLAN/segmentation allowed lateral movement; CERT-UA recommended VLAN/physical segmentation to contain spread.
Permissive or misconfigured firewall rules exposed SMB/NetBIOS ports (135/137/139/445), easing initial access and lateral spread.
Users/processes ran installers with administrative rights, enabling installation of rootkit components and persistent services.

title: AMD, Apple, Qualcomm GPUs leak AI data in LeftoverLocals attacks

vulnerabilities: GPU local memory is not cleared between kernel invocations, leaving residual data that can be recovered by subsequent kernels.
An attacker runs a “listener” kernel that reads uninitialized local memory, which still contains data written by a prior “writer” kernel.
GPU frameworks fail to enforce isolation between kernels/tenants, allowing one process to read another process’s local memory contents.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Leaked local-memory residues reveal sensitive ML/LLM artifacts (inputs, outputs, weights, intermediate computations) to unauthorized co-resident users.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: Local GPU memory intended to be private to a kernel invocation is exposed to other user contexts in multi-tenant environments.

title: Chinese hackers exploit VMware bug as zero-day for two years

vulnerabilities: vCenter Server (CVE-2023-34048) contained an out-of-bounds write that led to vmdird crashes and enabled remote code execution, exploited as a zero-day for initial access.
VMware Tools authentication bypass (CVE-2023-20867) allowed attackers to skip authentication for host/guest operations, enabling privilege escalation and data exfiltration from guest VMs.
Fortinet FortiOS zero-day (CVE-2022-41328) used path traversal to manipulate the filesystem, facilitating compromise of FortiGate devices and installation of custom implants.

title: Ukraine remains Russia’s biggest cyber focus in 2023

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)
vulnerabilities: FROZENLAKE abused reflected XSS on multiple Ukrainian government websites to inject scripts that redirected users to credential‑phishing pages.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command (OS Command Injection)
vulnerabilities: FROZENBARENTS exploited Exim mail server RCE flaws to execute commands, compromise mail servers, and use them for access, phishing distribution, and operational infrastructure.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: After compromising web servers, attackers uploaded a PHP webshell and Adminer to maintain persistence and directly access/exfiltrate databases, indicating insufficient restrictions on placing executable files on the server.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Victims were lured to install “fake Windows updates” from look‑alike domains; lack of verification of code authenticity/integrity enabled execution of the Rhadamanthys stealer.
Reliance on password‑only authentication for webmail and other accounts meant credential‑phishing (email/SMS spoofing of Telegram, Ukroboronprom, CPC, etc.) could directly yield unauthorized access.

title: Initial access broker repurposing techniques in targeted attacks against Ukraine

vulnerabilities: Exploitation of CVE-2022-30190 (Follina) via malicious RTF/HTML that invoked ms-msdt to execute code, reflecting insufficient validation of inputs passed to MSDT.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: PowerShell and installers fetched and executed code (IcedID, Cobalt Strike DLLs/MSIs) from attacker-controlled URLs (e.g., blinkin.top, 84.32.190.34) without verifying integrity/signature.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Opening malicious Excel XLL add-ins and EtterSilent-built documents that load and run external code/DLLs directly from attacker infrastructure.
Installation of unsigned or improperly signed MSI/EXE payloads masquerading as Microsoft updates (e.g., KB2533623.msi), indicating lack of signature enforcement for code/installers.
Trust placed in spoofed communications and domains (starlinkua.info, microsoftua.com, gov.uz.ua) and “official” update lures without strong verification of sender/domain or content authenticity.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
vulnerabilities: Security decisions (opening attachments, enabling add-ins, running installers from cloud links like Dropbox/Google Cloud Storage) based on untrusted, easily spoofed indicators such as email sender/display name and familiar hosting platforms.

title: Internet Explorer 0-day exploited by North Korean actor APT37

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
vulnerabilities: Incorrect JIT optimization in IE’s jscript9.dll caused a type confusion bug that allowed attacker-controlled JavaScript to achieve arbitrary code execution (root cause of CVE-2022-41128).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: The Office document loaded a remote RTF template and then remote HTML from attacker-controlled servers, causing IE to render untrusted content and enabling delivery of the exploit.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Remote templates/HTML were fetched and used without integrity/authenticity verification, allowing malicious code to be introduced via the template loading mechanism.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Reliance on the deprecated Internet Explorer/JScript engine inside Office exposed users to IE engine 0-days even when IE was not the default browser.

title: Russian threat group COLDRIVER expands its targeting of Western officials to include the use of malware

vulnerabilities: The “Proton-decrypter.exe” was presented as a benign decryption utility but actually installed the SPICA backdoor.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Targets were convinced to execute software retrieved from cloud storage outside the organization’s trust boundary.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Victims downloaded and ran a “decrypter” without verifying its integrity or provenance, enabling arbitrary code execution.
Impersonation accounts and “encrypted” PDFs were trusted without authenticating the sender or document, facilitating phishing and malware delivery.
SPICA steals browser cookies (session tokens), indicating authentication secrets stored client-side are accessible and reusable by user-mode malware.
Stolen cookies can continue to grant access if web sessions are long-lived or not bound to device/context, enabling session hijacking.
SPICA achieved persistence by creating a scheduled task via PowerShell; weak restrictions on who/what can create auto-run tasks allowed durable persistence.

title: Exposing initial access broker with ties to Conti

vulnerabilities: MSHTML 0-day (CVE-2021-40444) allowed crafted Office documents/markup to trigger ActiveX loading and remote code execution due to insufficient validation of untrusted content.
Adversaries spoofed domains (e.g., changing TLDs to .us/.co/.biz) and impersonated real employees to pass as trusted senders in spear-phishing.
Targets and security controls trusted file-sharing notification emails (WeTransfer/OneDrive, etc.) as authentic without independently verifying the sender or file provenance.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Victims retrieved ISO/DLL payloads from public file-sharing services and executed them without signature or integrity verification, enabling BazarLoader/BUMBLEBEE execution.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: Legitimate file-sharing platforms permitted uploading and sharing of dangerous files (e.g., ISO with LNK/DLL), facilitating malware distribution.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Workflow caused Office/MSHTML or Windows to load and execute ActiveX/DLL components sourced from attacker-controlled servers or mounted ISOs.
Limited or ineffective monitoring of unusual events (mass file-sharing notifications, ISO mounts, LNK executions) allowed human-operated phishing and payload delivery to evade detection.

title: Phishing campaign targets YouTube creators with cookie theft malware

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Targets were lured to download and run “demo” software from attacker-controlled sites or documents without verifying publisher/signature, resulting in execution of cookie-stealing malware.
Victims trusted forged business emails and cloned websites/social media pages impersonating legitimate companies, failing to verify the authenticity of counterparties and download sources.
Stolen session cookies remained valid long enough for hijackers to reuse them (“pass-the-cookie”), with inadequate revalidation/invalidation after suspicious activity or context change.

Sensitive account/channel actions (e.g., channel transfer, high-impact changes) were allowed based on an existing session, enabling attackers with stolen cookies to perform them without step‑up reauthentication (mitigated later by hardened workflows).
Accounts without MFA were more easily compromised via phishing and credential theft, enabling initial account takeover before stronger 2SV was enforced.
Session cookies (credential equivalents) were accessible to user-space processes; commodity stealers running under the user context could extract them from the local browser storage.
Non-persistent “smash-and-grab” malware left minimal artifacts; limited endpoint/account telemetry and retrospective visibility delayed user notification and detection of past compromise.

title: 0-days exploited by commercial surveillance vendor in Egypt

vulnerabilities: Delivery of the exploit via MITM on plaintext HTTP allowed the attacker to intercept and modify traffic, injecting redirects to attacker-controlled sites.
Use of HTTP (unencrypted) enabled interception and manipulation of web traffic, facilitating exploit injection without user interaction.
CVE-2023-41991 — a certificate validation flaw used in the chain, enabling trust/certificate checks to be bypassed as part of the attack.
CVE-2023-41992 — local privilege escalation in the XNU kernel to elevate code execution from app/user space to higher privileges.
CVE-2023-41993 — Safari/WebKit processing of web content lacked proper validation, enabling remote code execution when the target visited the attacker’s page.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
vulnerabilities: CVE-2023-4762 — Chrome renderer memory-safety issue exploited for initial RCE on Android (obtained as the renderer bug in the Android chain).

title: Countering threats from Iran

vulnerabilities: A UK university website was compromised and used to host a phishing kit, indicating insufficient controls preventing unauthorized modification/hosting of site content.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: The hijacked site hosted attacker-controlled phishing content, consistent with weak or missing restrictions on what files or scripts could be uploaded/placed on the server.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
vulnerabilities: Campaigns forced targets through redirects (incl. Google Sites pages masquerading as forms) and link shorteners to land on phishing domains, abusing unvalidated/unsafeguarded redirectors to add legitimacy and evade filters.

Account takeover succeeded once passwords and 2FA codes were phished, reflecting reliance on phishable factors rather than phishing-resistant authentication that binds credentials to the origin/device.
Credentials and one-time codes were harvested via phishing pages, showing dependence on shared secrets that are not protected against interception/reuse outside the legitimate authentication context.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Private Personal Information ('Privacy Violation')
vulnerabilities: Phishing pages exfiltrated visitor IPs, user-agents, and locales via Telegram, disclosing device/behavioral data to unauthorized actors.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Spyware disguised as a VPN was distributed outside the Play Store; users installing from untrusted platforms without signature/integrity verification could execute malicious code on their devices.

title: New Iranian APT data extraction tool

vulnerabilities: Reuse of previously hijacked/harvested session cookies to access webmail without re-authentication indicates sessions that remain valid long enough (and are not strongly bound) to be abused.
Accounts without MFA enabled were accessible with only stolen passwords, allowing HYPERSCRAPE to log in and exfiltrate data using acquired credentials.
The tool communicates with its C2 over HTTP and posts host and activity details in cleartext, exposing sensitive system and operational data to interception.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Information Exposure Through Query Strings in GET Request
vulnerabilities: The tool sends control values (e.g., identity strings, “OK” beacons) in URL query parameters, which can be logged or intercepted, leaking operational metadata.
Downloaded emails are written as .eml files to disk without encryption, leaving sensitive contents exposed at rest on the attacker’s machine or any intermediate staging host.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
vulnerabilities: Later versions “obfuscate” the hardcoded C2 with Base64, which is reversible encoding rather than cryptography, providing no real protection of sensitive strings.
Reliance on in-inbox security notifications that an attacker can delete hampers detection by the victim; lack of robust, out-of-band alerting/monitoring allows stealthy account abuse.

title: Magniber ransomware actors used a variant of Microsoft SmartScreen bypass

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities: SmartScreen/shdocvw.dll treats errors from signature parsing as a non-blocking condition and proceeds with the default action (run without warning), enabling a fail-open bypass via crafted malformed Authenticode signatures.

The SmartScreen warning mechanism for MotW files can be bypassed due to its design/implementation failing under certain error conditions, allowing untrusted downloads (MSI/JScript) to execute without security prompts.

Inadequate validation of PKCS#7/ASN.1 structures (e.g., missing signer certificate referenced by SignerInfo; corrupted SPC_INDIRECT_DATA_OBJID NID) leads to unexpected parser states that trigger the fail-open path instead of being safely rejected.

The Authenticode verification logic does not robustly enforce signature integrity and required fields; malformed or inconsistent signatures cause errors that result in skipping protections rather than conclusively treating the file as untrusted.

title: Active North Korean campaign targeting security researchers

vulnerabilities: A malicious file exploited a 0-day in a popular software package to execute shellcode, consistent with memory-corruption bugs in file parsers that allow arbitrary code execution.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: The standalone “GetSymbol” tool downloads and executes code from an attacker-controlled domain without verifying integrity or authenticity.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: The tool incorporates externally hosted functionality at runtime by fetching executable content from an attacker-controlled server.
The ostensibly benign utility contains hidden functionality to retrieve and execute attacker-supplied payloads, enabling covert compromise.

title: Spyware vendors use 0-days and n-days against popular platforms

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (‘Type Confusion’)
vulnerabilities: Type confusion used for remote code execution in WebKit JIT and Chromium (CVE-2022-42856 on iOS; CVE-2022-3723 and CVE-2022-4262 on Chrome/Samsung Internet Browser).
Pointer Authentication Code (PAC) mitigation bypass in iOS WebKit chain via DYLD_INTERPOSE technique, allowing continuation of the exploit chain despite mitigations.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: Sandbox escape/bypass enabling code to execute outside intended containment (AGXAccelerator sandbox escape CVE-2021-30900; Chrome GPU sandbox bypass CVE-2022-4135; Chrome sandbox escape CVE-2022-3038).
Kernel/driver privilege escalation to system/kernel level (ARM Mali/Android GPU drivers CVE-2022-38181 and CVE-2022-22706; AGXAccelerator privilege escalation aspect of CVE-2021-30900).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization (‘Race Condition’)
vulnerabilities: Linux kernel sound subsystem race condition granting kernel read/write (CVE-2023-0266).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Kernel information leak bugs used to aid kernel exploitation (ARM CVE-2023-26083; Samsung CVE-2023-21492).
Intent handling/redirection weaknesses in browsers leading to unintended navigation or exploitation paths (technique analogous to Chrome intent validation issues like CVE-2022-2856).

Exploitation of n-days due to delayed patch adoption by vendors (e.g., ARM Mali CVE-2022-38181 and CVE-2022-22706 fixes not yet incorporated; Samsung Browser on older Chromium lacking recent mitigations).

title: Analyzing a watering hole campaign using macOS exploits

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
vulnerabilities: XNU mach port type confusion (CVE-2021-30869) letting attackers change port types (e.g., to IKOT_HOST_PRIV/HOST_SECURITY), forge tokens, escape the sandbox, and escalate to root.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
vulnerabilities: WebKit memory corruption used for RCE in the browser (e.g., CVE-2021-1789 on macOS, CVE-2019-8506 on iOS) to gain initial code execution.
Kernel flaw allowed local privilege escalation to root and sandbox escape, enabling the payload to run with elevated privileges.
Gatekeeper was bypassed by removing the quarantine attribute from the downloaded payload, defeating execution checks.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Compromised websites embedded iframes loading attacker-controlled scripts/exploits from external servers (watering hole delivery).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: The exploit chain downloaded and executed a second-stage payload from a C2 using a provided URL/size without verifying integrity or authenticity.
Reliance on outdated/vulnerable WebKit/Safari versions enabled exploitation of an n-day (CVE-2021-1789) on targets that had not yet applied patches.

title: Government-backed actors exploiting WinRAR vulnerability

vulnerabilities: Inconsistent handling of filenames between WinRAR (normalizes/removes trailing spaces when writing) and Windows ShellExecute (treats extensions with spaces as invalid and applies default executable extension search), resulting in unintended execution of a .cmd file.

WinRAR’s extraction/open logic does not robustly validate crafted archive entries (e.g., filenames/directories with space-padded or space-in-extension names), allowing extraneous temp file expansion and unsafe invocation paths.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Names for Files and Other Resources
vulnerabilities: Acceptance and processing of filenames with trailing spaces or spaces in extensions (invalid/ambiguous on Windows) leads to name confusion that attackers exploit to trigger execution of a different file than the one selected.

When ShellExecute can’t parse the extension (due to spaces), it searches the target directory for default executable extensions (.cmd/.exe/etc.) and runs the first match, effectively searching an attacker-influenced directory.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: External Control of File Name or Path
vulnerabilities: Attackers control archive entry names and directory structure (e.g., a directory matching a file name) to influence what WinRAR extracts and what ShellExecute ultimately executes.
DLL sideloading in the ISLANDDREAMS chain (ImagingDevices.exe loading malicious STI.dll from %ProgramData%\Microsoft\DeviceSync) abuses Windows DLL search order to load attacker-supplied libraries.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Continued deployment of outdated WinRAR versions after a fix was released enables n‑day exploitation by threat actors, reflecting weak patch hygiene/use of outdated components.

title: Zimbra 0-day used to target international government organizations

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
vulnerabilities: Reflected XSS in Zimbra where the st URL parameter was inserted into the page without sanitization, allowing attacker-supplied script execution.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
vulnerabilities: The application failed to escape the st parameter before rendering it into an HTML attribute; the vendor fix explicitly added output escaping.
The campaign that stole the Zimbra authentication token via XSS indicates the token was readable by client-side script (e.g., a cookie lacking HttpOnly or token exposed to JS), enabling exfiltration.

title: The BadPilot campaign: Seashell Blizzard subgroup conducts multiyear global access operation | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: Authentication bypass in internet-facing apps (e.g., ConnectWise ScreenConnect CVE-2024-1709 and JetBrains TeamCity CVE-2023-42793) enabled pre-auth access and arbitrary command execution to install RMM agents.
Fortinet FortiClient EMS (CVE-2023-48788) SQLi was abused to invoke xp_cmdshell and run OS commands, providing initial code execution and persistence.
Microsoft Exchange ProxyShell component (CVE-2021-34473) allowed front-end request routing to privileged back-end services, leading to code execution and web shell deployment.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)
vulnerabilities: Zimbra (CVE-2022-41352) arbitrary file write via crafted attachments and Openfire (CVE-2023-32315) path traversal to setup/admin endpoints enabled web shell placement or admin takeover.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: After gaining write/RCE, the actor uploaded web shells (e.g., LocalOlive ASPX, primitive Zimbra shells) to maintain persistence and C2.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)
vulnerabilities: Modified OWA sign-in pages with rogue JavaScript to exfiltrate usernames/passwords as users authenticated.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere
vulnerabilities: Microsoft Outlook (CVE-2023-23397) forced the client to access attacker-controlled UNC paths, leaking NTLM credentials for privilege escalation/lateral movement.
JBOSS exploitation (CVE unknown) likely leveraged common JBoss/JMX deserialization RCE patterns to obtain command execution on internet-facing servers.
Credential theft via LSASS dumping (reg.exe/procdump) and subsequent exfiltration (rclone) indicates credentials were obtainable in recoverable form, enabling lateral movement.

Long-lived persistence using legitimate RMM tools and Tor hidden services (ShadowLink) went undetected, suggesting inadequate logging/monitoring of service installs, outbound Tor traffic, and admin actions.

title: StilachiRAT analysis: From system reconnaissance to cryptocurrency theft | Microsoft Security Blog

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Storing Passwords in a Recoverable Format
vulnerabilities: Chrome’s saved credentials are stored using reversible encryption (DPAPI), allowing StilachiRAT running in the user’s context to decrypt and exfiltrate usernames and passwords.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information in a Mechanism without Access Control
vulnerabilities: Sensitive data (passwords, crypto keys, seed phrases) resides in globally accessible mechanisms like the clipboard and user “Desktop/Recent” files, enabling the RAT to read and exfiltrate it.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: The RAT collects and transmits system reconnaissance data, active window titles, software inventory, and wallet extension details to a C2, exposing sensitive environment and user information.

Abuse of Windows Service Control Manager and registry for persistence, and access to other sessions’ resources, indicates insufficiently enforced ACLs on critical OS objects that allow unauthorized manipulation when a host is compromised.

StilachiRAT adjusts privileges (e.g., for shutdown/reboot), manipulates registry keys, and duplicates tokens to impersonate users, reflecting weak least-privilege enforcement and privilege boundary controls.

Running the RAT as a Windows service (commonly with elevated accounts like LocalSystem) grants broad system control and facilitates persistence and log-clearing that would be unnecessary under least-privilege execution.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: The RAT opens Explorer processes in other RDP sessions and duplicates their security tokens, indicating that security tokens and session-bound resources can be accessed across boundaries by a process with obtained privileges.
Event logs are easily cleared by the malware; lack of tamper-resistant or centralized logging reduces the ability to detect, investigate, and recover from compromise.

Anti-forensics and sandbox/analysis evasion by the RAT demonstrate that existing defenses (sandboxing, behavioral detection, egress controls) are not effectively enforced, allowing security mechanisms to be bypassed.

title: New Russia-affiliated actor Void Blizzard targets critical sectors for espionage | Microsoft Security Blog

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
vulnerabilities: Successful password spray against cloud identities indicates insufficient throttling/lockout or rate-limiting on sign-in attempts.
Password spraying and credential stuffing succeeded due to users having weak/guessable passwords.
Reliance on single-factor or phishable MFA methods enabled access with stolen credentials; lack of phishing-resistant authentication (e.g., FIDO2/passkeys).
Evilginx AitM phishing captured credentials and session cookies, which were replayed to bypass MFA and gain access.
Captured session tokens/cookies remained valid long enough for bulk data exfiltration; sessions not promptly invalidated after risky sign-ins.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
vulnerabilities: Overly broad mailbox and file-share permissions let a compromised user read other users’ mailboxes/folders via delegated access.
Default directory read permissions in Entra ID enabled tenant-wide enumeration (users, groups, roles, devices) via tools like AzureHound.
Inadequate mailbox auditing and monitoring of Graph/Exchange activity impeded detection of non-owner mailbox access and anomalous API usage.

title: Financially motivated threat actors misusing App Installer | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: The ms-appinstaller protocol handler was enabled by default, unnecessarily exposing a high-risk install path that attackers abused until Microsoft disabled it by default.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: App Installer fetched and executed MSIX packages from attacker-controlled remote URLs supplied via ms-appinstaller links, effectively including untrusted code into the system.
Using the ms-appinstaller URI allowed threat actors to bypass defense-in-depth controls such as SmartScreen and browser executable download warnings.

The trust decision for MSIX installs relied too heavily on package signing/format without robust reputation/legitimacy checks, enabling distribution of malicious but signed MSIX packages posing as legitimate apps.
Microsoft Teams meeting chats allowed unsolicited messages from external tenants (used by Storm-1674) to reach users without the usual accept/block gating, enabling phishing and malware delivery.

title: Cadet Blizzard emerges as a novel and distinct Russian threat actor | Microsoft Security Blog

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement ('Expression Language Injection')
vulnerabilities: Initial access via Confluence OGNL injection (CVE-2021-26084) to execute server-side code.
Exploitation of Microsoft Exchange (e.g., CVE-2022-41040, ProxyShell chain) using SSRF to pivot to internal services and gain code execution.
Local privilege escalation (e.g., pkexec/Polkit CVE-2021-4034) to obtain higher privileges on compromised hosts.
Authentication bypass weakness exploited in environments vulnerable to Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) to compromise domain trust.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Internet-facing services (Confluence, Exchange, CMS) left unpatched/outdated, enabling exploitation of known CVEs for initial access.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: Ability to place and run web shells (e.g., P0wny, reGeorg, PAS/WSO) on web servers due to insufficient validation or arbitrary file write.
Theft of credentials from LSASS dumps and registry hives enabling lateral movement with valid accounts.
Remote access accounts configured without MFA increased susceptibility to credential compromise and persistence.
Event logs (e.g., sec.evtx, sys.evtx) could be exfiltrated and cleared without effective detection/tamper protection, hindering incident response.
Security controls (e.g., Microsoft Defender AV) could be disabled via utilities/registry changes, undermining built-in defenses.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
vulnerabilities: Lack of egress controls allowed generic tunnels (Netcat, GOST, ngrok) and C2 over arbitrary sockets to attacker infrastructure.
Overly permissive remote administration paths (e.g., WMI/PSExec) and service permissions facilitated lateral movement once credentials were obtained.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Large-scale exfiltration of mail, documents, and SSH keys from servers enabled leak operations (e.g., “Free Civilian”).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Targeting IT service providers to access downstream government customers reflects exploitation of trust/supply-chain relationships (“compromise one, compromise many”).

title: Defending new vectors: Threat actors attempt SQL Server to cloud lateral movement | Microsoft Security Blog

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
vulnerabilities: A web application flaw allowed attackers to inject SQL, execute arbitrary queries, and gain initial access to the SQL Server.
The compromised application/DB account and/or SQL Server service ran with elevated rights, letting attackers enable xp_cmdshell, run OS commands, dump SAM/SECURITY hives, and create scheduled tasks.
The managed identity bound to the SQL Server VM had overly broad permissions in the cloud environment, enabling potential identity-based lateral movement once its token was obtained.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: Access tokens from the Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) were obtainable by any code running on the VM (including through SQL Server’s xp_cmdshell context), exposing credentials to a compromised process on the host.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
vulnerabilities: Database configuration controls (sp_configure/xp_cmdshell) and host resources were accessible to roles/accounts that did not need them, allowing attackers to change SQL Server settings and interact with critical OS resources.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Host, network, and database reconnaissance data—and potentially other outputs—were exfiltrated to an external service (webhook.site), indicating insufficient egress restrictions/monitoring to prevent data disclosure.

title: Diamond Sleet supply chain compromise distributes a modified CyberLink installer | Microsoft Security Blog

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: The modified installer downloads a second-stage payload from external URLs and decrypts/executes it in memory without validating its integrity or authenticity.
No cryptographic signature verification is performed on the downloaded second-stage payload (embedded in a PNG), allowing execution of tampered or attacker-controlled code.
A valid CyberLink code-signing certificate was used to sign the malicious installer, indicating compromise or misuse of signing keys or the signing process.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: The installer includes logic to retrieve and run functionality from attacker-controlled or compromised external domains (imgur, webville, github.io), placing execution under an untrusted sphere.

Legitimate CyberLink update infrastructure delivered the trojanized installer, implying insufficient access control/hardening in the software build/distribution pipeline that allowed unauthorized modification or hosting of malicious files.

The loader trusts content fetched over the internet (PNG-embedded payload) based on availability/decryption alone, without verifying the source’s authenticity beyond network transport, enabling content substitution by the attacker.

title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: Public-facing web/Java/SQL/VPN services were exploited via known input-validation flaws to achieve remote code execution and initial access.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: Vulnerable web applications allowed deployment of a web shell (e.g., China Chopper), enabling arbitrary server-side code execution.
Local privilege escalation using Juicy Potato/BadPotato exploited OS privilege/token handling to obtain SYSTEM-level access.

Disabling RDP Network Level Authentication (NLA) exposed pre-authentication interaction with the logon screen, enabling the Sticky Keys/IFEO debugger trick to run SYSTEM processes without prior user auth.

Credential stores (LSASS memory, SAM hive) were dumpable, allowing extraction/use of password hashes (e.g., pass-the-hash) due to lack of LSASS hardening (e.g., PPL, Credential Guard) and insecure WDigest settings.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Adversary downloaded and executed SoftEther VPN via certutil/bitsadmin without control over code provenance/integrity (no allowlisting or signature enforcement).

Over-permissive service creation and execution (via SCM) and highly privileged service accounts (e.g., SQL Server spawning system utilities and making network connections) enabled persistence and lateral actions.
Living-off-the-land activity and registry/RDP changes went undetected due to inadequate monitoring of critical events (e.g., registry key changes, anomalous RDP, LOLBin usage).
Reliance on valid single-factor credentials (no MFA) allowed sustained access and credential reuse across systems.
Stale/shared local administrator passwords facilitated lateral movement; mitigations cited include LAPS and password expiration policies.

title: Social engineering attacks lure Indian users to install Android banking trojans | Microsoft Security Blog

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Users are lured into sideloading APKs from WhatsApp/Telegram, installing untrusted code without integrity/signature verification.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
vulnerabilities: Fake apps impersonate legitimate banks/KYC apps with deceptive icons and screens to trick users into entering sensitive data.
The malicious app hides its launcher icon and continues running in the background to steal data and intercept SMS without user awareness.
Fraudulent “KYC/banking” apps request dangerous SMS permissions (RECEIVE_SMS, SEND_SMS) unnecessary for their stated purpose, enabling interception and exfiltration.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
vulnerabilities: Reliance on SMS-based OTPs and card grid values delivered/read on the same compromised device lets malware capture them and bypass MFA/transaction verification.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: PII and financial data (PAN/Aadhaar, DOB, addresses, bank/card details) are exfiltrated to attacker-controlled C2 and phone numbers.
Sensitive information (including OTPs and messages) is sent over SMS, an unencrypted channel, exposing contents to interception.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
vulnerabilities: Exfiltration endpoints like save_sms.php?phone= embed sensitive identifiers in URLs, risking leakage via logs, referrers, or intermediaries.
Victims trust spoofed bank communications and app branding on social platforms without verifying sender/app authenticity, enabling phishing and installation of malware.

title: Malware distributor Storm-0324 facilitates ransomware access | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: Exploitation of CVE-2023-21715 (Microsoft Publisher security feature bypass) to defeat Office security controls and execute malicious code despite policy.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Users are lured to SharePoint-hosted ZIPs containing JavaScript that downloads and runs a DLL (JSSLoader) without authenticity or integrity verification.
Permissive default settings (e.g., external access in Teams, domain creation in tenants) allow external entities to initiate chats and send attachments, increasing phishing exposure.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: Allowing external tenants to directly message internal users in Teams exposes internal users and data flows to untrusted parties who can deliver malicious links/files.
Reliance on phishable authentication (lack of phishing-resistant MFA) enables credential theft via email/Teams lures.
Excessive privileges and weak least-privilege enforcement (e.g., domain-wide admin/service accounts) magnify impact after initial access and facilitate ransomware deployment.
Endpoints with local administrative rights allow easy installation of RATs/malware dropped by the infection chain.
Not keeping Microsoft 365 auditing enabled and insufficient monitoring hinder detection, investigation, and containment of Storm-0324 activity.

Users and systems insufficiently verify the authenticity of external senders/content (invoice/payment lures mimicking DocuSign/QuickBooks; external “EXTERNAL” chats), enabling social engineering success.
Inadequate conditional access and unmanaged device controls allow external or low-trust contexts to access apps and deliver malicious content (e.g., via Teams and SharePoint) beyond intended policy.

title: Midnight Blizzard conducts targeted social engineering over Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: Reliance on phishable MFA (number matching/code entry) allowed the attacker to social‑engineer users over Teams to approve the sign‑in, resulting in successful authentication as the victim.

External collaboration/Teams settings allowed unsolicited chats from untrusted tenants; insufficient validation/allow‑listing of trusted organizations enabled spoofed “support” messages to reach users.
Actor created onmicrosoft.com subdomains using homoglyphs and security‑themed names (e.g., mlcrosoftaccounts.onmicrosoft[.]com) to visually spoof legitimate domains and deceive users.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
vulnerabilities: Use of password spray and brute force indicates controls did not sufficiently throttle or lock out excessive authentication attempts.
Password policies were weak enough that password spraying/brute force remained a viable initial access technique.

Ability for a compromised account to add/enroll a device and thereby satisfy Conditional Access “managed device” requirements suggests insufficient authorization/controls around device registration and compliance status.
Campaigns leveraging token theft indicate session tokens were long‑lived or insufficiently bound (e.g., not device‑bound), enabling reuse after capture.
Without Microsoft 365 auditing enabled, detection and investigation of malicious Teams messages, sign‑ins, and domain changes would be hindered.

title: New macOS vulnerability, Migraine, could bypass System Integrity Protection | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: A heritable SIP-bypass entitlement (com.apple.rootless.install.heritable) on systemmigrationd allowed its child interpreters (bash/perl) to execute with elevated/SIP-exempt privileges, enabling arbitrary code execution outside intended controls.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: External Control of System or Configuration Setting
vulnerabilities: Attackers with root set environment variables via launchctl (e.g., PERL5OPT) to control the behavior of privileged child processes, causing them to execute attacker-specified code while inheriting SIP bypass.
The overall design allowed bypassing System Integrity Protection during migration by leveraging entitled processes and interpreter behavior, undermining SIP’s enforcement and protections.

Presence of debug/hidden flags in Setup Assistant (-MBDebug, -ResumeBuddyYes) altered the operational workflow to perform migration without sign-out, facilitating automated exploitation paths that aid the SIP bypass.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Privileged interpreters (perl/bash) executed functionality influenced by attacker-controlled environment/options (e.g., PERL5OPT loading and invoking system()), effectively incorporating untrusted code into a SIP-exempt context.

title: Multiple North Korean threat actors exploiting the TeamCity CVE-2023-42793 vulnerability | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: TeamCity authentication bypass (CVE-2023-42793) allowed unauthenticated attackers to invoke critical functionality leading to remote code execution.
DLL search-order hijacking by placing malicious DSROLE.dll/Version.dll next to legitimate binaries (wsmprovhost.exe/clip.exe) so the executables load attacker-controlled DLLs from C

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Compromise of unpatched TeamCity servers (N-day exploitation) due to failure to promptly apply the vendor’s update/mitigations.
Credentials retrievable from LSASS memory post-compromise (e.g., in environments lacking protections like Credential Guard), enabling credential dumping and lateral movement.
TeamCity/service processes running with high privileges amplified impact of RCE, granting attackers system-level control for persistence and credential access.
ForestTiger backdoor uses a hard-coded decryption key (“uTYNkfKxHiZrx3KJ”) to decrypt its config, a cryptographic weakness observed in the attacker’s tooling.

title: Peach Sandstorm password spray campaigns enable intelligence collection at high-value targets | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: Accounts accepted weak/common passwords, enabling large-scale password spray success and initial access.
Legacy authentication without MFA allowed attackers to authenticate with only a password obtained via spraying.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
vulnerabilities: Insufficient lockout controls (e.g., missing/weak AD FS extranet lockout) enabled sustained password spray attempts.
Active sessions (cookies) could remain valid after password resets, letting attackers retain access post-compromise.
Internet-facing Zoho ManageEngine and Confluence instances were left unpatched against known RCE flaws and were remotely exploited.
ManageEngine SAML processing weakness (CVE-2022-47966) allowed signature verification bypass leading to unauthenticated RCE.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement (Expression Language Injection)
vulnerabilities: Confluence OGNL injection (CVE-2022-26134) enabled remote code execution on exposed servers.
DLL search order hijacking via a legitimate VMware executable to load attacker-controlled DLLs.
AD FS private signing keys were stealable, enabling Golden SAML (forging SAML tokens to access cloud resources).
Excessive/unguarded privileges let the actor create new Azure subscriptions, alter MFA settings, and onboard Azure Arc clients for persistence.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
vulnerabilities: Lack of strict egress/allow-list controls allowed AnyDesk and custom tunnels (EagleRelay) to communicate with attacker infrastructure for C2 and lateral movement.

title: Star Blizzard increases sophistication and evasion in ongoing attacks | Microsoft Security Blog

cwe_entries.cwe_name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)
vulnerabilities: The campaign hides attacker domains behind legitimate websites that have open redirect parameters, chaining multiple redirects (e.g., link shorteners + open redirectors) to evade detection.
Evilginx performs adversary-in-the-middle to capture authentication cookies/MFA tokens and replays them to access targets’ mailboxes without needing the victim present.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking
vulnerabilities: Target services accept stolen session cookies (and MFA-bearing tokens) without binding them to the original client/device or context, enabling reuse from the attacker’s infrastructure.
Session tokens remain valid long enough after login that once captured via AiTM they can be reused to immediately access accounts, even when MFA is enabled.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
vulnerabilities: Altered, legitimate-looking OneDrive share notifications and PDF lures present “Open” buttons and branding that misrepresent the true destination (attacker redirector), tricking users into authenticating.

Recipients and some controls trust superficially legitimate artifacts (e.g., Safe Links-wrapped URLs copied by the actor, lookalike sender identities/templates) without robust verification of origin and link integrity.

Security controls are bypassed through technique layering—password-protected PDFs, nested link shorteners, Safe Links cloaking, and server-side filtering to defeat scanners—indicating gaps or ineffective deployment of anti-phishing and URL inspection.

title: Flax Typhoon using legitimate software to quietly access Taiwanese organizations | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: Initial access by exploiting known flaws in public-facing web/Java/SQL/VPN services to achieve remote code execution and drop a web shell.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: Deployment of the China Chopper web shell on compromised servers, enabled by server-side flaws that allow writing or uploading executable script files.
Local privilege escalation to SYSTEM using Juicy Potato/BadPotato and related token/COM abuse to obtain higher privileges on Windows.
Disabling RDP Network Level Authentication (NLA) weakens pre-authentication enforcement, allowing interaction with the logon screen and facilitating unauthorized access with compromised accounts.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel
vulnerabilities: Abusing the Sticky Keys/IFEO “debugger” registry trick to launch Task Manager as SYSTEM from the Windows sign-in screen before authenticating.
Undermining built-in security controls (e.g., turning off NLA, modifying critical registry keys, lack of LSASS PPL/Guard) to bypass or weaken intended defenses.
Credential theft by dumping LSASS memory and the SAM hive; weak configuration such as WDigest UseLogonCredential enables recovery of credentials for offline cracking and pass‑the‑hash.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Exfiltrating password hashes and other authentication material from LSASS/SAM, exposing sensitive information that enables further access and lateral movement.

title: Multiple North Korean threat actors exploiting the TeamCity CVE-2023-42793 vulnerability | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: CVE-2023-42793 in TeamCity allowed an authentication bypass that enabled unauthenticated remote code execution on exposed servers.
DLL search-order hijacking by placing malicious DSROLE.dll/Version.dll next to copied wsmprovhost.exe/clip.exe in C
Organizations ran vulnerable versions of the TeamCity server (an N‑day issue), enabling initial compromise until patches/mitigations were applied.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Post-exploitation payloads were fetched and executed via PowerShell from remote URLs without signature/integrity verification, allowing arbitrary code to run.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in Memory
vulnerabilities: Credentials present in LSASS memory were dumped after compromise, exposing sensitive authentication material stored in readable form.
The ForestTiger malware used a static embedded key (“uTYNkfKxHiZrx3KJ”) to decrypt its configuration, illustrating a hardcoded key in the scenario’s tooling.

title: Volt Typhoon targets US critical infrastructure with living-off-the-land techniques | Microsoft Security Blog

vulnerabilities: Reliance on single-factor “valid credentials” enabled unauthorized sign-ins from unusual IPs; lack of MFA allowed attackers to authenticate like normal users.
The Fortinet-associated AD/service account had excessive privileges and usable logon rights, enabling LSASS dumping, use of ntdsutil to create DC installation media, and lateral movement.
Credentials in LSASS memory and browser stores were accessible to attackers (absent LSASS PPL/Credential Guard), allowing hash/credential theft for persistence and reuse.
Offline cracking of NTDS password hashes was feasible, indicating weak password complexity/rotation policies and enabling reentry with recovered domain credentials.

Internet exposure of SOHO router/firewall/VPN HTTP/SSH management interfaces and permissive remote admin protocols (e.g., WMI/PSExec) expanded the attack surface and enabled proxying/lateral movement.

Missing or unenforced hardening controls (e.g., LSASS PPL, Credential Guard, attack surface reduction rules, egress/host firewall controls) allowed LOLBins, netsh portproxy, and C2 tooling to operate undetected.
Limited behavioral monitoring and logging made living-off-the-land, hands-on-keyboard activity hard to detect, delaying identification and response to credential theft and network discovery.

title: Agonizing Serpens (Aka Agrius) Targeting the Israeli Higher Education and Tech Sectors

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Unpatched/vulnerable internet-facing web servers were exploited for initial access (e.g., Exchange-class issues like ProxyShell/ProxyLogon), indicating outdated or unmaintained software.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: Attackers deployed ASPX web shells (e.g., ASPXSpy variants), consistent with insufficient file upload validation allowing executable content to be placed on the server.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
vulnerabilities: SMB password spraying and brute-force attempts suggest lack of account lockout/rate-limiting controls on authentication services.
Successful/attempted credential attacks via spraying/brute force indicate inadequate password complexity/rotation policies.
Credential dumping (LSASS/Mimikatz, SAM hive) shows secrets were accessible in memory/on disk without adequate protections (e.g., Credential Guard, disabling WDigest, LSASS protection).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
vulnerabilities: Attempts to modify EDR service dependencies imply service configuration permissions allowed or were targeted for unauthorized changes.
BYOVD use of vulnerable kernel drivers (GMER, Rentdrv2) exposed privileged IOCTLs enabling termination of protected processes, reflecting insufficient access control in driver operations.
Extracted PII was staged and archived from C
Reliance on local Windows Event Logs allowed attackers to delete logs (DeleteLogs), impeding detection/forensics due to lack of robust centralized/immutable logging.

Broad access to databases and internal hosts after foothold (lateral movement via Plink; DB extraction with sqlextractor) indicates insufficient authorization/segmentation controls limiting what a compromised account or system could reach.

title: Hacking Employers and Seeking Employment: Two Job-Related Campaigns Bear Hallmarks of North Korean Threat Actors

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Candidates are convinced to clone/install attacker-controlled NPM packages from GitHub during interviews, importing BeaverTail/InvisibleFerret into developer machines.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Malicious packages and scripts (e.g., NPM packages, Python/AnyDesk payloads) are installed/executed without signature or hash verification, enabling code execution from attacker infrastructure.
Lack of verification that GitHub repositories, packages, and purported employers are legitimate (e.g., vague/anonymous ads, repos flagged by issues) leads to accepting tampered content.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
vulnerabilities: Security-relevant decisions (running code for an “interview,” granting access to applicants) are based on unverifiable inputs like resumes, GitHub profiles, and VoIP interviews.
Employers’ onboarding/hiring processes insufficiently authenticate remote applicants’ real identities, allowing Wagemole actors using fake or borrowed identities to gain positions and access.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: Using company-issued computers for personal/job-search activities exposes corporate assets to an untrusted sphere, enabling malware to bridge into enterprise environments.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Trust placed in minimally maintained or single-repository GitHub accounts/components increases supply chain risk, as attackers host or inject malicious code in such packages.
Reliance on security tooling that does not adequately analyze Node/NPM package execution allowed malicious packages to evade detection and establish C2/backdoor functionality.

title: BlackCat Climbs the Summit With a New Tactic

vulnerabilities: The ISO and /app/config store sensitive data (e.g., chat access token, victim credentials, URLs) without encryption, as explicitly noted by “NO CONFIG ENCRYPTION.”
The VM boot process sets the root password from a predefined value embedded in the ISO; access tokens/credentials are also embedded in the image.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
vulnerabilities: Strings in the controller are obfuscated with a single-byte XOR, a trivially reversible/weak technique.
Running the ransomware inside a customized VM evades host-based controls that lack VM introspection, defeating expected security protections.
Lateral movement and remote execution over SMB/ADMIN$ indicate insufficient restrictions on remote admin shares and service creation across hosts.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
vulnerabilities: Writable/executable SMB/CIFS shares allow the malware to copy and execute payloads remotely (smb_copy_and_exec.py, psexec/wmiexec).
Credentials are stored/handled insecurely (in config; harvested via tools like mimikatz, secretsdump), enabling reuse for lateral movement.

Use of ntlmrelayx and related tools suggests environments susceptible to NTLM relay/pass-the-hash due to weak/misconfigured authentication (e.g., lack of signing), enabling unauthorized actions with relayed credentials.

title: Blitz Malware: A Tale of Game Cheats and Code Repositories

vulnerabilities: The backdoored game cheat executables secretly fetch and install the Blitz downloader/bot while still running the real cheats, hiding malicious functionality inside legitimate-looking software.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: The attacker uploads and serves Windows DLLs and an XMRig miner via Hugging Face Spaces, which allows arbitrary executable content to be hosted and distributed as part of the C2.
A C2 API endpoint exposed the full list of registered infections without authentication, allowing researchers (and anyone) to retrieve victim data and bot inventory.
After redirection from the hf.space endpoint, bot registration and command traffic is sent over HTTP to 176.65.137.44, exposing GUID, username, and other data in cleartext.

The update logic compares the local DLL hash to a SHA256 value fetched from Pastebin and then downloads from paste.rs; the “integrity check” relies on unauthenticated, attacker-controlled sources rather than a trusted signature.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
vulnerabilities: The campaign uses RC4 to protect the miner payload and 1‑byte XOR “encryption” for strings, both providing weak protection that is easily reversible.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
vulnerabilities: The keylogger stores captured keystrokes, program names, and timestamps in plaintext at %temp%\RestartManager.log, leaving sensitive data exposed on disk.

title: CL0P Seeds ^_- Gotta Catch Em All!

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
vulnerabilities: The MOVEit Transfer zero-day exploited by CL0P was an SQL injection flaw that enabled initial compromise, privilege escalation, and installation of a web shell to exfiltrate data.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
vulnerabilities: After exploiting MOVEit, the attackers deployed and executed a web shell on the server to run arbitrary code and automate data theft (referenced by “Anti-Webshell Protection”).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Terabytes of stolen corporate data were exfiltrated and then publicly released via Tor and BitTorrent, exposing confidential information to anyone.
The seed infrastructure used FTP to stage and move stolen files; FTP transmits credentials and content in cleartext, risking interception or tampering over untrusted networks.
The seeding servers’ FTPS services presented self-signed TLS certificates (example.ru); clients that accept these without proper validation are susceptible to spoofing or man-in-the-middle attacks.

title: Threat Brief: Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966

vulnerabilities: Specially crafted pre-auth requests cause the device to read beyond intended memory bounds (“bleed”), returning memory contents that include session tokens.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: The memory disclosure exposes sensitive data (e.g., session tokens) to unauthenticated attackers, enabling unauthorized access.
Stolen session tokens remain valid and reusable for session hijacking; the need to terminate active sessions after patching indicates inadequate invalidation/expiration of existing sessions.

title: Conti Ransomware Gang: An Overview

vulnerabilities: Lack of MFA allowed phished credentials to grant immediate access to email, VPN, or admin interfaces.
“Unprotected” internet-facing applications and services exposed sensitive functions/resources without sufficient authorization checks.
Public-facing applications were exploitable (e.g., via injection/validation flaws), enabling initial remote code execution.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
vulnerabilities: Overly permissive SMB/Windows Admin shares and shared content enabled lateral movement and tainting of shared files.
Excessive privileges/weak separation let attackers escalate rights, stop services, and delete Volume Shadow Copies to inhibit recovery.
Susceptibility to DLL injection allowed malware to load into legitimate processes (defense evasion via T1055.001).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Data exfiltration used for “double extortion” indicates insufficient controls preventing unauthorized access and leakage of sensitive files.

title: CryptoClippy Speaks Portuguese

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Users are lured to download WhatsApp.zip/.exe from attacker-controlled sites (via malvertising/SEO) and execute it without verifying integrity, enabling initial compromise.
