Lack of enforcement to verify digital signatures/code-signing on the downloaded installers/scripts lets unsigned or forged binaries (e.g., .lnk/.ps1/.exe) run.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Executing a shortcut (.lnk) that launches obfuscated PowerShell and reflectively loads an attacker-supplied EXE (“sc”) incorporates untrusted functionality into the system.
Workflow/apps accept pasted crypto destination addresses without authenticity checks (e.g., address book, out-of-band confirmation), allowing clipboard-swapped addresses to be used for transactions.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
vulnerabilities: Very long wallet addresses are displayed/handled in ways users cannot practically verify, so a swapped address looks legitimate and the change goes unnoticed.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)
vulnerabilities: The loader injects the stealer into svchost.exe via syscalls/CreateRemoteThread; insufficient protections against code injection into system processes are exploited.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
vulnerabilities: Malware achieves persistence by writing a .lnk into the user’s Startup folder and creating scheduled tasks, indicating overly permissive autostart/task-creation permissions that can be abused.
RC4-encrypted PowerShell backdoor scripts modify Terminal Services/RDP registry settings and create local accounts, showing inadequate access control/hardening that allows such configuration changes.
Attack scripts clear Windows event logs; absence of immutable/centralized logging and robust monitoring enables attacker stealth and hampers detection/response.

title: Diplomats Beware: Cloaked Ursa Phishing With a Twist

vulnerabilities: Targets trusted seemingly legitimate embassy-themed emails/attachments without independently verifying authenticity, enabling spear-phishing lures (BMW flyer, earthquake guidance) to succeed.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
vulnerabilities: Links in the lure use URL shorteners (tinyurl, t.ly) to redirect victims to attacker-controlled/co‑opted sites that deliver payloads, exploiting trust in redirections.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
vulnerabilities: Malicious files are disguised to look harmless (LNK files masquerading as .PNG images; “e‑yazi.docx.exe” with whitespace to appear as a document), tricking users into executing malware.
DLL search order hijacking/sideloading via a legitimate executable (windoc.exe/WinWord.exe) loading attacker-provided DLLs (e.g., APPVISVSUBSYSTEMS64.dll, MSVCP140.dll) from the current directory.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: HTA/ISO payloads are downloaded from co-opted legitimate sites and executed without cryptographic verification or provenance checks, allowing execution of untrusted code.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Attackers likely accessed a recipient’s mailbox or related infrastructure to obtain the legitimate BMW flyer and unpublished email addresses, enabling highly credible lures and broader targeting.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: Reliance on external/free webmail services for embassy group inboxes outsources security and expands the attack surface, reducing organizational visibility and control over threat monitoring.

title: CloudKeys in the Air: Tracking Malicious Operations of Exposed IAM Keys

vulnerabilities: AWS IAM access keys were committed to public GitHub repositories, allowing automated scanners to harvest them within minutes.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Sensitive IAM credentials were exposed in public repo files and commit history, making them accessible to anyone, including threat actors.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
vulnerabilities: Overly-permissive IAM policies on the leaked credentials enabled creation of EC2 instances, security groups, and cross-region operations, violating least-privilege.
Credentials were stored in plaintext (or trivially encoded) and not managed as short‑lived/rotated secrets, lacking preventive controls before and after exposure.
Inadequate auditing/monitoring (e.g., lack of repo clone event visibility and insufficient cloud anomaly detection) would hinder timely detection of credential abuse.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities: The cloud environment allowed rapid, large-scale provisioning of high-cost EC2 instances across regions without effective quotas, guardrails, or budget controls, enabling cryptojacking.

title: Exploring a Critical Risk in Google Workspace's Domain-Wide Delegation Feature

vulnerabilities: GCP principals with token‑minting permissions can generate access tokens for a domain‑wide delegated service account and escalate to impersonate any Google Workspace user within granted scopes.

Authorization to act on behalf of Workspace users is effectively granted based solely on the service account’s domain‑wide delegation, without sufficiently validating whether the calling GCP principal is authorized to perform user impersonation.
The default Compute Engine service account commonly has Editor by default and automatic role grants, creating an overly permissive baseline that enables the attack path.

Granting domain‑wide delegation to a service account residing in a project where many identities have rights (e.g., Editor or token‑creator) assigns powerful impersonation capabilities to the wrong place/principal set.

Coarse project‑level permissions (e.g., Service Account Token Creator) allow minting tokens for highly sensitive, domain‑wide delegated service accounts, reflecting a mismatch between permission scope and operation impact.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: Domain‑wide delegation bridges GCP and Google Workspace so that Workspace user data becomes accessible to GCP identities outside the intended administrative sphere, enabling lateral movement and data access across the boundary.

title: Over the Kazuar’s Nest: Cracking Down on a Freshly Hatched Backdoor Used by Pensive Ursa (Aka Turla)

vulnerabilities: Kazuar’s steal/unattend tasks target files like Windows unattend.xml and various app/config artifacts that store credentials and tokens in readable/plaintext formats, enabling easy exfiltration.

Saved credentials and access tokens for cloud apps, browsers, Signal, and Git SCM are retrievable from local storage without robust protection (e.g., not strongly encrypted/bound to device/user), facilitating credential theft and reuse.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
vulnerabilities: Sensitive artifacts (config files, registry locations, app data) are accessible to standard user contexts, allowing the injected backdoor to read secrets and modify autorun/persistence points.
Weak controls around inter-host mechanisms (named pipes, WMI/DCOM, remote registry/shares) allow P2P tasking, remote command execution, and lateral movement once any valid user context is obtained.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: Legitimate WordPress sites were hijacked to host C2 (e.g., PHP in wp-content/wp-includes paths), likely via insecure file upload/plugin flaws that let attackers place executable server-side files.
Over-privileged user/service contexts enable process injection (e.g., into explorer.exe), creation of scheduled tasks/services, and registry-based persistence without needing additional exploits.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
vulnerabilities: The malware’s use of HMAC-MD5 and simplistic Caesar-cipher string “encryption” reflects weak/legacy crypto choices that, while aiding attacker stealth, are cryptographically fragile and analyzable.
Limited or ineffective endpoint/network logging and telemetry allow stealthy multistage execution, named-pipe C2, and anti-analysis evasion to proceed with low detection probability.

title: Lampion Is Back With ClickFix Lures

cwe_entries.cwe_name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
vulnerabilities: Fake tax-authority-themed pages and “ClickFix” prompts misrepresented actions as benign fixes, tricking users into copying and running malicious PowerShell commands.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: The PowerShell command and subsequent stages downloaded and executed code (VBS/DLL) from remote servers without signature or integrity verification.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: The attack chain incorporated and executed functionality (VBS stagers and a DLL loader) obtained from attacker-controlled cloud endpoints.
Users and systems trusted lookalike domains and files without verifying authenticity, enabling execution of attacker-provided commands and content.
Abuse of powerful system utilities (PowerShell, rundll32) by untrusted scripts enabled arbitrary code execution and loading of a malicious DLL.
The malware created hidden scheduled tasks and wrote autostart files in the Startup folder, indicating insufficient restrictions/monitoring on persistence mechanisms available to non-admin users.
Stage 3 exfiltrated a victim identifier via HTTP GET parameters to C2 infrastructure, sending data in cleartext.
Malicious content was disguised as legitimate tax-related documents/installers and scripts (e.g., VBS delivered via .php endpoints, loader named to appear benign).
Heavily obfuscated, bloated VBScript stages embedded malicious logic that performed reconnaissance, evasion, and staging actions.
Multi-stage, highly obfuscated execution, dispersed process chains, and oversized binaries (e.g., 700+ MB DLL) bypassed or degraded traditional detection and analysis mechanisms.

title: Threat Group Assessment: Muddled Libra (Updated May 16, 2025)

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
vulnerabilities: Helpdesk workflows allowed password and MFA resets based on weak caller verification, enabling account takeover via social engineering.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
vulnerabilities: MFA “push bombing” succeeded due to lack of throttling, lockout, or alerting on repeated MFA prompts.
Phishable MFA (OTP/push) and acceptance of captured codes from 0ktapus pages allowed attackers to authenticate as users.
Corporate credentials cached on BYOD/personal devices were harvested by infostealers (e.g., Raccoon, RedLine).
Attackers searched registries, local drives, and shares for cleartext “password” artifacts, indicating plaintext secrets stored in files/scripts/configs.
Over-privileged endpoints and accounts (e.g., cached admin creds, service accounts) enabled rapid privilege escalation (Mimikatz, DCSync, Impacket).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
vulnerabilities: Excessive AD/EDR permissions (e.g., replicate directory changes, EDR console admin) let attackers perform DCSync and clear security alerts.
Limited network segmentation enabled RDP-based lateral movement across business segments with minimal detection.
Ability to install and operate multiple unsanctioned RMM tools, create external mailbox forwarding rules, and modify security tool configs.
Security controls (AV/EDR/firewalls) were disabled or uninstalled, indicating inadequate tamper protection and hardening.
Unmanaged/unsupervised cloud VMs, rotating proxies, mailbox rule changes, and RMM activity were insufficiently logged/monitored, aiding evasion.

title: P2PInfect: The Rusty Peer-to-Peer Self-Replicating Worm

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
vulnerabilities: CVE-2022-0543 (Lua sandbox escape in Debian/Ubuntu-packaged Redis) enables execution of attacker-controlled Lua that loads libraries and runs arbitrary OS commands for RCE.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: Large numbers of Redis instances are reachable from the public internet, exposing the database service to untrusted networks and enabling remote exploitation attempts.
Weak or missing access controls on Redis (e.g., insufficient network ACLs or authentication) allow remote clients to reach and exercise powerful commands like EVAL, facilitating exploitation.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: After initial access, infected hosts auto-download and execute additional payloads from a P2P C2 network, allowing controllers to push new code/functions into running systems.
Follow-on malware samples (e.g., linux, windows, miner, winminer) were observed being fetched in plaintext over HTTP, enabling interception/tampering of transferred binaries.

title: Over the Kazuar’s Nest: Cracking Down on a Freshly Hatched Backdoor Used by Pensive Ursa (Aka Turla)

vulnerabilities: Multiple targeted artifacts (e.g., Windows unattended files, Git/Cloud app configs, browser stores) keep tokens/credentials in readable/plaintext files that Kazuar’s steal/unattend tasks exfiltrate.
Credentials and session secrets for browsers, cloud apps, source control, and messaging are stored or cached with weak protection accessible to user‑space malware.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
vulnerabilities: Lax file/registry ACLs on credential stores and autorun/persistence locations allow a non‑admin implant to read sensitive data and modify persistence points.

Insufficient restriction of WMI, named pipe endpoints, and local script engines (PowerShell/VBS/JS) enables arbitrary code execution, lateral tasking, and C2 over local IPC without adequate authorization checks.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
vulnerabilities: The actor can deliver and execute attacker‑supplied PowerShell/VBScript/JavaScript/.NET methods on hosts, abusing unrestricted dynamic code execution paths.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: The “upgrade” command fetches and executes new payloads without code signing or integrity verification, mirroring a class of weakness also present in insecure enterprise tooling.
Kazuar embeds a fixed RSA public key and a hard‑coded GUID used across samples (for task encryption/cookies), leading to key/material reuse.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
vulnerabilities: The variant uses HMAC‑MD5 and a Caesar‑style cipher for strings; these weak algorithms aid defenders’ analysis and are not cryptographically sound.
Injection into over‑privileged or broadly trusted processes (e.g., browser, svchost) and permissive task/service creation lets the implant perform actions beyond least privilege.
Lack of comprehensive monitoring of script execution, WMI, autoruns, file integrity, and named pipe usage allows Kazuar’s stealth (timestomping, anti‑analysis, userland injection) to evade detection.

title: Chinese PlugX Malware Hidden in Your USB Devices?

vulnerabilities: DLL side-loading via x32dbg.exe loading x32bridge.dll from the current working directory, allowing an attacker-placed malicious DLL to be loaded first.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: The signed x32dbg host process loads attacker-supplied DLLs and encrypted payloads (.dat) from attacker-controlled folders (including USB), executing untrusted code.
Unsigned x32bridge.dll is accepted and executed by a signed process; lack of module-signature enforcement enables execution of untrusted code next to trusted binaries.
Use of Unicode NBSP (U+00A0) in directory names prevents Windows Explorer/cmd.exe from properly rendering/showing folders, enabling malware to hide files on USB media.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
vulnerabilities: Malware uses desktop.ini with CLSIDs and icons to make folders appear as drives/recycle bin and crafts .lnk files named like the USB volume, deceiving users into executing the payload.

title: Inside SnipBot: The Latest RomCom Malware Variant

cwe_entries.cwe_name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
vulnerabilities: Malware masquerades as a PDF (EXE with PDF icon/name) and a fake Adobe download page to trick users into executing the downloader.
Over-trust in Authenticode-signing allowed a stolen/spoofed code-signing certificate to lend legitimacy to the downloader; defenses likely did not enforce publisher reputation/revocation checks.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Initial downloader retrieves and executes additional EXE/DLL stages from attacker C2 (unsigned, in-memory) without verifying integrity or authenticity.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection')
vulnerabilities: COM hijacking via attacker-controlled HKCU\Software\Classes\CLSID\...\InprocServer32 causes explorer.exe to load and run attacker’s keyprov.dll.

Side-loading/hijacking behavior where Windows components (e.g., explorer/rundll32) load DLLs from user-writable locations (e.g., %LOCALAPPDATA%\KeyStore, DataCache), enabling persistence and execution of malicious modules.
keyprov.dll opens a TCP listener on port 1342 that accepts and executes command strings without any apparent authentication.
Default ability for standard users to register per-user COM objects (HKCU) that are auto-loaded by explorer.exe enables persistence without elevated rights.

Lack or misconfiguration of defense-in-depth controls (e.g., application control blocking rundll32/unsigned modules, strict egress filtering, blocking SCP/LOLBins) allowed execution, C2, and exfiltration.

title: Fake CVE-2023-40477 Proof of Concept Leads to VenomRAT

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
vulnerabilities: CVE-2023-40477 in WinRAR enables RCE when a crafted archive is opened, consistent with a memory-safety parsing flaw leading to code execution.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
vulnerabilities: The base PoC code reused by the attacker targets GeoServer CVE-2023-25157, a SQL injection vulnerability.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: The fake PoC and its PowerShell stages download and execute code (bat/ps1/exe) from http

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: The PoC embeds logic to fetch and run external scripts/binaries controlled by the attacker (remote batch/PowerShell and EXE), effectively including untrusted functionality at runtime.
The campaign relies on users trusting a newly posted GitHub PoC and accompanying video/README without validating provenance or authenticity, enabling execution of a trojanized PoC.

title: Apache ERP Zero-Day Underscores Dangers of Incomplete Patches

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel
vulnerabilities: Attackers bypassed authentication by targeting other non-XML-RPC endpoints after the patch removed only the XML-RPC interface, allowing unauthorized access via alternate paths.
The flaw allowed unauthenticated users to trigger internal requests through OFBiz endpoints, enabling SSRF.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: The authentication bypass enabled access to sensitive information within applications using the OFBiz framework.
The initial patch addressed a single vector (removing XML-RPC) without fixing the underlying auth logic, resulting in an incomplete fix that attackers could bypass.

title: Microsoft: Russia's Sandworm APT Exploits Edge Bugs Globally

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
vulnerabilities: Zimbra CVE-2022-41352 was abused to write files outside intended directories (e.g., into the webroot) via archive extraction, enabling web shell placement and RCE.

Microsoft Exchange CVE-2021-34473 (part of ProxyShell) involved URL/path confusion that bypassed normal access controls pre-auth, enabling access to backend functionality and facilitating RCE when chained.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: External Control of File Name or Path
vulnerabilities: Microsoft Outlook CVE-2023-23397 allowed an attacker-controlled UNC path in a message property to be automatically accessed by Outlook, triggering an SMB connection and leaking NTLM credentials for relay.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
vulnerabilities: Fortinet FortiClient EMS CVE-2023-48788 is an unauthenticated SQL injection that attackers used to gain code execution on the EMS server.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel
vulnerabilities: ConnectWise ScreenConnect CVE-2024-1709 enabled bypassing normal authentication (e.g., via installer/setup paths), allowing attackers to create or obtain administrative access without valid credentials.

title: Iranian APT 'BladedFeline' Hides in Network for 8 Years

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities: Internet-facing web server flaw allowed upload of a web shell, enabling execution of attacker-controlled code.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
vulnerabilities: Server exploit enabled arbitrary code execution (deployment of backdoors like Shahmaran/Whisper and reverse shells).

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Malicious IIS module (“PrimeCache”) was loaded into IIS, adding untrusted functionality for covert access/persistence.
Shahmaran backdoor communicated with C2 without encryption, exposing command/data traffic in cleartext.
Inadequate logging/monitoring enabled the APT to remain undetected in the environment for up to eight years.
Weak controls permitted placement and auto-start of malware from the Startup directory and execution of tools (e.g., PowerShell) for persistence and lateral movement.

title: Critical Bluetooth Flaw Exposes Android, Apple & Linux Devices to Takeover

vulnerabilities: Attacker emulates a Bluetooth HID keyboard and tricks the host state machine into pairing without user confirmation, gaining trusted input capability.
The Bluetooth stack accepts pairing from an unauthenticated device due to flaws in the pairing flow, enabling a fake keyboard to be trusted.
Systems allow a newly paired HID keyboard to inject keystrokes without requiring explicit user approval or policy checks, granting it full user-level actions.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Verification of Source of a Communication Channel
vulnerabilities: The host does not sufficiently verify that the Bluetooth connection originates from a legitimate, previously approved keyboard before establishing a trusted HID channel.
On Linux/BlueZ, a prior mitigation existed but was disabled by default, leaving devices vulnerable out of the box despite available fixes.
Platform defenses (e.g., Apple Lockdown Mode) are bypassed by the unauthenticated HID pairing, failing to enforce intended security controls against malicious peripherals.

title: Comcast Xfinity Breached via CitrixBleed; 35M Customers Affected

vulnerabilities: CitrixBleed leaked memory contents (e.g., session tokens) from NetScaler ADC/Gateway due to a memory read beyond intended bounds, enabling token theft.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Attackers obtained sensitive data (usernames, hashed passwords, PII, security Q/A) after exploiting CitrixBleed, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of customer information.
Even after patching, active session tokens in memory could be reused to hijack sessions; failure to invalidate existing/persistent tokens allowed authentication bypass.
Reliance on a Citrix component with a known, actively exploited vulnerability (CVE-2023-4966) and incomplete/timing-related mitigation led to compromise.

title: Ferret Malware Added to 'Contagious Interview' Campaign

cwe_entries.cwe_name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
vulnerabilities: Attackers use a fake interview process and an executable posing as a Google Chrome update to deceive users into installing malware.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Victims are led to download and run “virtual meeting” software from attacker-controlled links without verifying authenticity or integrity, enabling execution of malicious shell scripts and droppers.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: The attack chain loads and executes untrusted components (JavaScript BeaverTail dropper and Python InvisibleFerret backdoor) delivered from attacker infrastructure.
Signature-based defenses (Apple XProtect) failed to detect newer “FlexibleFerret” variants, allowing malware to bypass endpoint protection.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: Malware harvests sensitive data from web browsers and crypto wallets, exfiltrating information to threat actors.

title: A New, Spookier Gh0st RAT Malware Haunts Global Cyber Targets

vulnerabilities: Malicious JavaScript is embedded in Windows LNK shortcut files inside archives, installing the DLL payload while showing a decoy document.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
vulnerabilities: LNK files and decoy documents are crafted to appear benign, tricking users into executing the shortcut and launching the malware.
Targets open and execute unverified archives/shortcuts from phishing emails, lacking checks such as trusted signatures or provenance validation.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: The system executes code (JavaScript/DLL payloads) sourced from untrusted email attachments, incorporating untrusted functionality into execution.
Once running, the RAT can access the camera, keystrokes, files, and event logs, indicating insufficient restriction of process capabilities and device/resource access.
Small protocol/header changes (e.g., altered magic bytes) allow the malware to evade signature-based detection, revealing reliance on brittle detection mechanisms.
Attackers can erase local event logs; without protected/centralized, tamper-evident logging, this defeats forensic visibility.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: The RAT’s capabilities (keylogging, screenshots, file exfiltration, system inventory) enable theft of sensitive data due to inadequate data protection on endpoints.

title: Google Patches Another Chrome Zero-Day as Browser Attacks Mount

vulnerabilities: CVE-2023-6345 — integer overflow in Chrome’s Skia graphics library that can be triggered via a malicious file, leading to memory corruption and potential sandbox escape from the renderer process.
CVE-2023-4863 — heap out-of-bounds write in the libwebp (WebP) image decoder, allowing crafted images to corrupt memory and enable code execution across multiple browsers.
CVE-2023-5217 — heap out-of-bounds write in libvpx (VP8) used by Chromium-based browsers, exploitable via crafted media/WebRTC to achieve memory corruption and potential code execution.

title: Evasive Jupyter Infostealer Campaign Showcases Dangerous Variant

vulnerabilities: Trust decisions were made solely because the malware was digitally signed with valid certificates, allowing initial execution without adequately verifying publisher identity/reputation or revocation status.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Victims were enticed via SEO poisoning, redirects, and drive-by downloads to retrieve installers and payloads without independent integrity/authenticity validation before execution.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Executing InnoSetup-based installers and loaders obtained from untrusted web sources introduced attacker-controlled functionality onto endpoints.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
vulnerabilities: Malicious executables used document-like, trustworthy file names to masquerade as benign content and trick users into launching them.
Browser password managers, VPN/RDP apps, and crypto-wallet data were stored/accessible in a way that a local user-context process (the malware) could extract them once running.
Users with administrative privileges increased the infostealer’s ability to backdoor the host, execute PowerShell, and persist, amplifying impact once executed.

title: Attackers Exploit 6-Year-Old Microsoft Office Bug to Spread Spyware

vulnerabilities: Microsoft Office Equation Editor memory-corruption (CVE-2017-11882) triggered by a crafted Excel/Office file enables arbitrary code execution.
The Equation Editor fails to validate lengths/fields in embedded object data, allowing malformed input to corrupt memory and lead to RCE.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
vulnerabilities: Continued use of older, unpatched Microsoft Office versions exposes systems to a long-known, patched RCE vulnerability.
Users opening malicious documents while logged in with administrator rights allows full system takeover once RCE is achieved.
Credentials stored by browsers/mail/FTP clients can be extracted by malware running in the user’s context (e.g., Agent Tesla credential theft).

title: Microsoft Outlook Zero-Click Security Flaws Triggered by Sound File

vulnerabilities: Outlook’s security feature failed to properly verify whether a URL for a custom reminder sound was in a trusted zone (local/intranet), allowing retrieval from untrusted Internet/SMB locations.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: Outlook allowed a custom sound to be loaded from an attacker-controlled UNC/SMB path, pulling untrusted content into the client’s execution environment.

Microsoft’s patch logic (using MapUrlToZone) was bypassable (including via a single-character tweak), resulting in incomplete mitigation and enabling continued abuse of the custom reminder sound feature.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
vulnerabilities: Windows Media Foundation’s sound file parsing flaw (CVE-2023-36710) allowed crafted audio to trigger memory corruption leading to remote code execution when autoplayed.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities: The earlier Outlook issue (CVE-2023-23397) enabled coercing the client to authenticate to an attacker SMB server via a remote sound file, leaking the user’s password hash (Net-NTLM).

title: Qantas Airlines Breached, Impacting 6M Customers

vulnerabilities: Attackers accessed a call center platform containing PII (names, emails, phone numbers, birth dates, frequent flyer numbers) for ~6M customers.

Unauthorized access via the third-party call center platform suggests insufficient access restrictions/segmentation and led to exposure of customer data; Qantas added access control measures only after the incident.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: Storing and making PII accessible within a third-party service provider’s environment expanded the trust boundary and exposed data outside Qantas’ direct control.
The post-incident addition of “monitoring” indicates prior gaps in audit/logging that could hinder timely detection of abnormal data access.

title: Threat Group Using Rare Data Transfer Tactic in New RemcosRAT Campaign

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
vulnerabilities: The .lnk → HTA → PowerShell chain pulls and executes functionality (6.hta, word_update.exe) from an attacker-controlled domain.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
vulnerabilities: Payloads are fetched and run without integrity verification, allowing tampered or malicious code (RemcosRAT) to be installed.
No enforcement of code-signing for scripts/binaries enables execution of unsigned HTA/PowerShell content and the RemcosRAT loader.
Abuse of risky built-in utilities (mshta.exe, PowerShell, other Windows native binaries/LOLBins) to retrieve and execute remote code.

cwe_entries.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
vulnerabilities: Sensitive data is moved over anonymous pipes between processes, exposing it to a malicious child process and enabling covert exfiltration.
Security controls (EDR/AV, script/LOLBIN restrictions) failed to block or detect the IPC-based exfiltration and living-off-the-land execution.
Limited monitoring/telemetry on IPC channels and script interpreter activity allowed the pipe-based data transfer and staged downloads to evade alerts.
